etymology: The English Bible keeps Jordan as the river of crossing and of washing. Webster 1828 prints no JORDAN lemma on the fetched 1828 page this tick (related/cookie only) — this page does not invent one. Companion pages already treat baptism, covenant, and zion. This page fills the KJV-gap common of the river God dries, and the river in which the Son is baptized.
biblical_def: Jordan in Scripture is not a scenic border and not a private spa. It is the river the LORD dries so His people pass clean over, and the river in which John baptizes and the Son comes to be baptized. The priests that bare the ark stood firm on dry ground in the midst of Jordan until all the people were passed clean over (Jos 3:17). The LORD dried up the waters of Jordan as He did the Red sea (Jos 4:23). Naaman dipped himself seven times in Jordan and his flesh came again like a little child (2Ki 5:14). Jesus cometh from Galilee to Jordan unto John, to be baptized of him (Mat 3:13). He was baptized of John in Jordan (Mar 1:9). The dictionary therefore keeps Jordan from becoming either tourism or a brand. God opens the water, or you do not cross.

Mat 3:13
Then cometh Jesus from Galilee to Jordan unto John, to be baptized of him.
Mar 1:9
And it came to pass in those days, that Jesus came from Nazareth of Galilee, and was baptized of John in Jordan.
corruption_summary: Jordan is corrupted when the crossing is recast as self-help, when baptism is sold as a lifestyle dip, and when the river is kept as scenery while the LORD who dries it is dropped.
corruption_paragraphs: The first corruption is Jordan as tourism. Joshua 3:17 is priests and an ark on dry ground, not a hike with a view. The age keeps the river and drops the covenant.
The second corruption is Jordan as a wellness dip. Naaman is not a spa story. He went down and dipped seven times according to the saying of the man of God (2Ki 5:14). Sentiment is not cleansing.
The third corruption is baptism without the Son. Matthew 3:13 is Jesus coming to Jordan unto John. Mark 1:9 is baptized of John in Jordan. A brand named Jordan is not that baptism.

etymology: Webster 1828 treats BEGIN (preterit began; participle begun) from Latin genero / gigno: to have an original or first existence; to take rise; to commence; to do the first act; to enter upon something new. He cites Luke 1, 1 Peter 4:17, 1 Samuel 3:12, and Genesis 11:6. This page fills the KJV-gap common of the first act. Companion pages already treat repent.
biblical_def: Began in Scripture is not a self-start and not a motivational kickoff. It is the first act God names, or the first act men take under His eye. Then began men to call upon the name of the LORD (Gen 4:26). When men began to multiply on the face of the earth, the next chapter is not progress but the flood's threshold (Gen 6:1). From that time Jesus began to preach, and to say, Repent: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand (Mat 4:17). The former treatise is of all that Jesus began both to do and teach (Act 1:1). The man healed began to publish it much (Mar 1:45). The dictionary therefore keeps began from becoming a brand of hustle. God begins, or the beginning is only noise.
webster_summary: Webster 1828 defines BEGIN, preterit began: to have an original or first existence; to take rise; to commence; to do the first act; to enter upon something new. He cites Luke 1, 1 Peter 4:17, 1 Samuel 3:12, Genesis 11:6.
webster_full: BEGIN', verb intransitive preterit tense began; participle passive begun. [Latin genero, gigno.]
1. To have an original or first existence; to take rise; to commence.
As he spake by the mouth of his holy prophets, who have been since the world began. Luke 1.
Judgment must begin at the house of God. 1 Peter 4:17.
2. To do the first act; to enter upon something new; to take the first step.
BEGIN every day to repent.
When I begin I will also make an end. 1 Samuel 3:12.
And this they begin to do. Genesis 11:6.
scriptures: Gen 4:26
And to Seth, to him also there was born a son; and he called his name Enos: then began men to call upon the name of the LORD.
Gen 6:1
And it came to pass, when men began to multiply on the face of the earth, and daughters were born unto them,
Mat 4:17
From that time Jesus began to preach, and to say, Repent: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.
Act 1:1
The former treatise have I made, O Theophilus, of all that Jesus began both to do and teach,
Mar 1:45

But he went out, and began to publish it much, and to blaze abroad the matter, insomuch that Jesus could no more openly enter into the city, but was without in desert places: and they came to him from every quarter.
corruption_summary: Began is corrupted when origin is recast as self-authorship, when Jesus beginning to preach is sold as a TED opener, and when multiplying on the earth is called progress without the next verse.
corruption_paragraphs: The first corruption is the self-made start. Genesis 4:26 is men beginning to call upon the name of the LORD, not a founder story. The age keeps the launch and drops the Name.
The second corruption is Jesus as a keynote. Matthew 4:17 is Jesus began to preach, Repent. Acts 1:1 is all that Jesus began both to do and teach. A brand opener is not that beginning.
The third corruption is multiplication as progress. Genesis 6:1 is men began to multiply — and the flood is at the door. Headcount is not holiness.

etymology: Webster 1828 prints WOMEN as noun plural of woman (pron. wimen; supposed from Sax. wifman). WOMAN he treats as a compound of womb and man: the female of the human race, grown to adult years, citing Genesis 2:22. This page fills the KJV-gap plural. Companion page already treats woman.
biblical_def: Women in Scripture are not a marketing segment and not an interchangeable class. They are daughters of Eve under the law of the LORD, called to modest apparel, to teach the young women to love husband and children, and to continue in prayer with the church. Women adorn themselves in modest apparel, with shamefacedness and sobriety (1Ti 2:9). They may teach the young women to be sober, to love their husbands, to love their children (Tit 2:4). The upper room continued with one accord in prayer and supplication, with the women, and Mary the mother of Jesus (Act 1:14). Miriam the prophetess went out, and all the women after her with timbrels (Exo 15:20). Favour is deceitful, and beauty is vain: but a woman that feareth the LORD, she shall be praised (Pro 31:30). The dictionary therefore keeps women from becoming either a slogan or a erasure. God made woman from the man, and He has not repealed the order.
webster_summary: Webster 1828 defines WOMEN as noun plural of woman (Sax. wifman supposed). WOMAN: the female of the human race, grown to adult years; a female attendant. He cites Genesis 2:22.
webster_full: WOMEN, noun plural of woman. pronoun wimen. But it is supposed the word we pronounce is from Sax. wifman, and therefore should be written wimen.
WOMAN, noun plural women. [a compound of womb and man.]
1. The female of the human race, grown to adult years.
And the rib, which the Lord god had taken from the man, made he a woman. Genesis 2:22.
Women are soft, mild, pitiful, and flexible.
2. A female attendant or servant.
scriptures: In like manner also, that women adorn themselves in modest apparel, with shamefacedness and sobriety; not with broided hair, or gold, or pearls, or costly array;
Tit 2:4
That they may teach the young women to be sober, to love their husbands, to love their children,
Act 1:14
These all continued with one accord in prayer and supplication, with the women, and Mary the mother of Jesus, and with his brethren.
And Miriam the prophetess, the sister of Aaron, took a timbrel in her hand; and all the women went out after her with timbrels and with dances.
Favour is deceitful, and beauty is vain: but a woman that feareth the LORD, she shall be praised.
corruption_summary: Women is corrupted when the sex is recast as a fluid brand, when modest apparel is mocked as oppression, and when the fear of the LORD is swapped for a feed of beauty.
corruption_paragraphs: The first corruption is erasure. Genesis 2:22 is woman made from the man. The age keeps the word women and empties the sex. A slogan is not a daughter of Eve.
The second corruption is fashion as liberation. 1 Timothy 2:9 is modest apparel, shamefacedness, sobriety. Titus 2:4 is young women taught to love husbands and children. The recovery is not a runway.
The third corruption is beauty as gospel. Proverbs 31:30 says favour is deceitful and beauty is vain: a woman that feareth the LORD shall be praised. The feed is not that fear.

etymology: Webster 1828 treats FAR as adjective and adverb [Latin porro]: distant; separated by a wide space; remote from purpose; remote in affection or obedience; alienated in a spiritual sense. Adverb: to a great extent or distance; in a great proportion. He cites Joshua 9:6, Matthew 25:14, Exodus 8:28, Proverbs 31:10, Philippians 1:23, and Ephesians 2:13. This page fills the KJV-gap common of distance God names and distance God closes. Companion pages already treat nigh and peace.
biblical_def: Far in Scripture is not a vibe of independence and not a travel brand. It is the distance of transgression removed, the alienation closed by blood, and the LORD far from the wicked. As far as the east is from the west, so far hath He removed our transgressions from us (Psa 103:12). Ye who sometimes were far off are made nigh by the blood of Christ (Eph 2:13). Peace to him that is far off, and to him that is near, saith the LORD (Isa 57:19). Thou art not far from the kingdom of God (Mar 12:34). The LORD is far from the wicked: but He heareth the prayer of the righteous (Pro 15:29). The dictionary therefore keeps far from becoming either wanderlust or a therapy of space. God removes, or you stay far.
webster_summary: Webster 1828 defines FAR as adjective: distant; remote from purpose; remote in affection or obedience; alienated. Adverb: to a great extent or distance; in a great proportion. He cites Joshua 9:6, Matthew 25:14, Exodus 8:28, Proverbs 31:10, Philippians 1:23, Ephesians 2:13.
webster_full: F'AR, adjective [Latin porro; Gr. connected with, a way, a passing, to pass or go. See Fare.]
1. Distant, in any direction; separated by a wide space from the place where one is, or from any given place remote.
They said, we are come from a far country. Joshua 9:6.
The kingdom of heaven is as a man travelling into a far country. Matthew 25:14.
3. Remote in affection or obedience; at enmity with; alienated; in a spiritual sense.
F'AR, adverb
1. To a great extent or distance of space.
Only ye shall not go very far away. Exodus 8:28.
5. In a great proportion; by many degrees; very much.
Who can find a virtuous woman? for her price is far above rubies. Proverbs 31:10.
Ye, who were sometime far off, are made nigh by the blood of Christ. Ephesians 2:13.
scriptures: As far as the east is from the west, so far hath he removed our transgressions from us.
Eph 2:13
But now in Christ Jesus ye who sometimes were far off are made nigh by the blood of Christ.
I create the fruit of the lips; Peace, peace to him that is far off, and to him that is near, saith the LORD; and I will heal him.
And when Jesus saw that he answered discreetly, he said unto him, Thou art not far from the kingdom of God. And no man after that durst ask him any question.
The LORD is far from the wicked: but he heareth the prayer of the righteous.
corruption_summary: Far is corrupted when distance is recast as authentic selfhood, when far-off is kept as a mood, and when the blood that makes nigh is swapped for a journey.
corruption_paragraphs: The first corruption is wanderlust as piety. Psalm 103:12 is transgression removed as far as east from west — God's act, not a gap year. The age keeps the miles and drops the mercy.
The second corruption is alienation as identity. Ephesians 2:13 is ye who were far off made nigh by the blood of Christ. A brand of outsider is not that far-off.
The third corruption is nearness without the kingdom. Mark 12:34 is not far from the kingdom of God. Proverbs 15:29: the LORD is far from the wicked. Sentiment is not arrival.

etymology: Webster 1828 treats THROUGHOUT as preposition (thruout': through and out): quite through; in every part; from one extremity to the other. Adverb: in every part. This page fills the KJV-gap common of the whole field God names. Companion pages already treat church and earth.
biblical_def: Throughout in Scripture is not a coverage metric and not a brand of ubiquity. It is the whole field the LORD fills with rest, fame, plague, or witness. The churches had rest throughout all Judaea and Galilee and Samaria, and were edified (Act 9:31). Joshua's fame was noised throughout all the country (Jos 6:27). The boil with blains is throughout all the land of Egypt (Exo 9:9). The man published throughout the whole city how great things Jesus had done unto him (Luk 8:39). They were all scattered abroad throughout the regions of Judaea and Samaria, except the apostles (Act 8:1). The dictionary therefore keeps throughout from becoming a dashboard. God fills the field, or the map is only ink.
webster_summary: Webster 1828 defines THROUGHOUT as preposition: quite through; in every part; from one extremity to the other. Adverb: in every part. The cloth was of a piece throughout.
webster_full: THROUGHOUT, preposition thruout'. [through and out.] Quite through; in every part; from one extremity to the other.
This is the practice throughout Ireland. A general opinion prevails throughout England.
throughout the whole course of his life, he avoided every species of vice.
THROUGHOUT, adverb throut'. In every part. The cloth was of a piece throughout.
scriptures: Act 9:31
Then had the churches rest throughout all Judaea and Galilee and Samaria, and were edified; and walking in the fear of the Lord, and in the comfort of the Holy Ghost, were multiplied.
Jos 6:27
So the LORD was with Joshua; and his fame was noised throughout all the country.
Exo 9:9
And it shall become small dust in all the land of Egypt, and shall be a boil breaking forth with blains upon man, and upon beast, throughout all the land of Egypt.
Luk 8:39
Return to thine own house, and shew how great things God hath done unto thee. And he went his way, and published throughout the whole city how great things Jesus had done unto him.
Act 8:1

And Saul was consenting unto his death. And at that time there was a great persecution against the church which was at Jerusalem; and they were all scattered abroad throughout the regions of Judaea and Samaria, except the apostles.
corruption_summary: Throughout is corrupted when the whole field is recast as market share, when rest throughout the churches is sold as a vibe, and when persecution throughout the regions is dropped from the map.
corruption_paragraphs: The first corruption is coverage as gospel. Acts 9:31 is churches at rest throughout Judaea and Galilee and Samaria, walking in the fear of the Lord. A dashboard is not that rest.
The second corruption is fame as self-brand. Joshua 6:27 is the LORD with Joshua, fame noised throughout the country. The age keeps the noise and drops the LORD.

The third corruption is a map without blood. Acts 8:1 is persecution, scattered throughout the regions. Luke 8:39 is published throughout the whole city what Jesus had done. Sentiment is not that field.
